title: Integer-Lattice Encoding of Riemann-Zeta Argand Loops: Persistence of Dirichlet Frequencies under Binary Geometric Quantization
description: A computational note on a binary integer-lattice encoding of consecutive Riemann-zeta Argand loops. Across 10,000 loops, the double-centered lattice tensor preserves a strong Dirichlet-frequency comb near omega = log m, with residual log(m/k) intermodulation structure and a 36.3% out-of-sample variance reduction under cross-fit removal of a predeclared known-frequency dictionary. The note also develops a local Nyquist interpretation of the scale T = 2*pi*m^2 and the reciprocal first-fold map m* = T/(2*pi*m), while explicitly distinguishing an identifiability boundary from a power-onset law. No claim of a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is made.
notes: Series subtitle: Reflections on the Riemann Hypothesis with Commander Sol: a human-AI computational note. AI assistance is disclosed in the package. Creator: Alex Malachevsky, ORCID 0009-0008-6009-3196.
